## Classical models: from averages to latent factors {.lesson-slide}

<div class="review-grid">
<div>
<p class="review-kicker">MODEL LADDER</p>
<table class="lesson-table review-table"><thead><tr><th>model</th><th>prediction</th><th>what it adds</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>Global mean</td><td>$\mu$</td><td>one number for everyone</td></tr>
<tr><td>User / item bias</td><td>$\mu+a_u$, $\mu+b_i$</td><td>generous users; popular items</td></tr>
<tr><td>Biased MF</td><td>$\mu+a_u+b_i+p_u^\top q_i$</td><td>latent user–item interaction</td></tr>
</tbody></table>
<p class="lesson-small">The ladder adds structure, not new data.</p>
</div>
<div class="review-stack">
<div class="review-card"><span>IMPLEMENTATION</span><b>sklearn estimator</b><p><code>fit(X, y)</code> → <code>predict(X_new)</code>; learned attributes end in <code>_</code>.</p></div>
<div class="review-card"><span>SELECTION</span><b><code>GridSearchCV</code></b><p><code>param_grid</code>, <code>cv</code>, <code>scoring=&quot;neg_root_mean_squared_error&quot;</code>, <code>refit=True</code>.</p></div>
<div class="review-card"><span>REPORT</span><b>validation → test</b><p>Choose on validation, open test once, keep the split fixed.</p></div>
</div>
</div>

<div class="lesson-flow tight review-flow">
<div>fit<br><b>learn parameters</b></div><i>→</i>
<div>predict<br><b>score pairs</b></div><i>→</i>
<div>validate<br><b>choose model</b></div><i>→</i>
<div>test<br><b>report once</b></div>
</div>

<p class="lesson-takeaway">The estimator workflow stays the same even when the prediction rule changes.</p>

## Neural models: learned interaction + side information {.lesson-slide}

<div class="review-grid">
<div>
<p class="review-kicker">MODEL LADDER</p>
<table class="lesson-table review-table"><thead><tr><th>model</th><th>interaction</th><th>what it adds</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>MFNet</td><td>$p_u^\top q_i$</td><td>ID embeddings + biases</td></tr>
<tr><td>NCF</td><td>$\mathrm{MLP}([p_u,q_i])$</td><td>learned nonlinear interaction</td></tr>
<tr><td>Two-tower</td><td>$f_u(p_u)^\top f_i(q_i)$</td><td>separate encoders; retrieval</td></tr>
<tr><td>Side-info blocks</td><td>MFNet + additive $g_m(\cdot)$</td><td>continuous, categorical, text, image</td></tr>
</tbody></table>
<p class="lesson-small">On the Amazon demo: text was the only clear gain; continuous, categorical, and image were flat or neutral.</p>
</div>
<div class="review-stack">
<div class="review-card"><span>NETWORK</span><b>PyTorch <code>nn.Module</code></b><p><code>__init__</code> defines layers; <code>forward</code> defines shapes and branches.</p></div>
<div class="review-card"><span>TRAINING</span><b>skorch</b><p><code>NeuralNetRegressor</code>: <code>fit</code>, <code>predict</code>, <code>history</code>; tune with <code>module__</code> parameters.</p></div>
<div class="review-card"><span>TUNING</span><b><code>GridSearchCV</code></b><p><code>module__K</code>, <code>module__hidden</code>; <code>train_split=False</code>, <code>cv=KFold(...)</code>, <code>refit=True</code>.</p></div>
</div>
</div>

<div class="lesson-flow tight review-flow">
<div>build<br><b>nn.Module</b></div><i>→</i>
<div>fit<br><b>skorch</b></div><i>→</i>
<div>tune<br><b>GridSearchCV</b></div><i>→</i>
<div>ablate<br><b>one block</b></div>
</div>

<p class="lesson-takeaway">Neural models change the interaction; side information adds blocks. Always ablate one block at a time.</p>
